evidence.title: Supplier qualification SQ-2016-005 - Nordpol Chemicals AB, NP-310 Dry
evidence.claim: In 2016, NP-310 Dry from Nordpol Chemicals AB replaced Polioli Sereni PS-400 for the TL-5 process.
evidence.quote: Replaces Polioli Sereni PS-400 for TL-5.

evidence.title: Laboratory report LT-2018-022 - water content of TL-5
evidence.claim: A 2018 lab report shows VD-1 drying is effective, while molecular sieve addition provides negligible water reduction.
evidence.quote: The molecular sieve addition reduces water by less than 0.002 % - not measurable

evidence.title: FATTURA / INVOICE n. 7620/25
evidence.claim: Polyol NP-310 Dry was still being purchased for the plant in October 2025.
evidence.quote: Item: Polyol NP-310 Dry, tank truck.

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-2001-014
evidence.claim: In 2001, molecular sieves were added to TL-5 to absorb residual water from polyol PS-400.
evidence.quote: add 2 kg molecular sieve 3A per batch to absorb residual water from polyol PS-400

evidence.title: DEVIATION REPORT DR-2001-019
evidence.claim: In 2001, water content in polyol PS-400 exceeding 0.05% caused CO2 formation and bulging cans for TL-5.
evidence.quote: cans bulging at a customer (domed lids). Carbon dioxide formed by the reaction of isocyanate with water.

evidence.title: Technical data sheet - TL-5 tank sealing compound
evidence.claim: In 2021, drying polyol below 0.05% water remained necessary to prevent CO2 formation from the reaction with isocyanate.
evidence.quote: The polyol must be dried below 0.05 % water: water reacts with isocyanate and forms CO2.

verdict.process_name: TL-5 tank sealing compound (1K moisture-cure polyurethane)
verdict.instruction: Charge 900 kg polyether polyol NP-310 Dry (RM-401) and dry under vacuum at 90 °C in VD-1 until water < 0.05 %.
verdict.reason: The step prevents CO2 formation and bulging cans caused by the reaction of isocyanate with water when polyol water content exceeds 0.05% (E8, E9). This hazard remains a quality and safety concern for the TL-5 process (E9).

chain.claim: Water content above 0.05% in polyol causes CO2 formation and bulging cans

dependencies.name: water reacting with isocyanate to form CO2

counter_evidence.claim: Molecular sieve addition provides negligible water reduction
counter_evidence.resolution: This supports the necessity of the vacuum drying step over alternative methods.
